flags.text: Every theme-aware colour reaches into the global AppDependencies.current.app.settingsManager singleton instead of the SwiftUI environment, so colour depends on hidden global state and views re-colour only when something else triggers a re-render.
File header says 'Blue primary (trust/calm), green accents', but AppTheme.accent is terracotta (coral red) and primary follows the user's colour theme.
Stored constants with no reference anywhere in the repo (grep AppTheme.<name> incl. tests): sand, success, heartRateColor, hfColor, vlfColor, secondaryLight, secondaryDark, smallPadding.

flags.text: Hard-codes 7.0/4.5/2.0 instead of RecoveryScoreConstants.ReadinessLabels thresholds and skips ReadinessScoring.tenScaleClamped, so a non-finite score is coloured 'Rest' (dustyRose) while readinessLabel maps it to the midpoint 5.0 ('Moderate'); thresholds can drift from the label.

units.does: Recovery score colour: delegates to ScoreVerdict(score:).color (Wong ladder 90/75/60/45/30).

HRV word: with a positive baseline, maps AnalysisSummaryGenerator.personalCategory(hrv/baseline) to Excellent/Good/Fair/Reduced/Low; otherwise absolute RMSSD tiers >=60 Excellent, >=45 Good, >=30 Fair, else Low.

flags.text: Absolute RMSSD cut-offs 60/45/30 ms are inline magic numbers with no age adjustment, used by SessionHRVDetailView without a baseline, while the same file's baseline path uses named StressNormativeConstants.

Without a baseline the label uses fixed 60/45/30 ms cut-offs, while "What This Means" (hrvCategory) uses the age-adjusted category; MorningResultsView passes nil baseline until baselineStats load and SessionHRVDetailView never passes one, so the same night gets two different HRV verdicts — the exact "third answer" the MorningResultsView comment says was removed.

units.does: HRV colour: baseline-relative categories excellent→sage, good→softGold, fair→terracotta, reduced/low→dustyRose; absolute tiers >=60 sage, >=45 softGold, >=30 terracotta, else dustyRose.
Text variant of hrvColor: switches on the returned Color by equality — sage→sageText, softGold→softGoldText, terracotta→terracottaText, anything else→dustyRoseText.

flags.text: Maps tiers by comparing SwiftUI Color values for equality; it works only while hrvColor returns exactly these static constants — any change there (opacity, theme-dependent colour) silently falls to the dustyRose default.
